challenge: Track A run cost ($75k/yr, $1.98/grant at 70k grants) omits registry-specific operating costs that Unbound's own requirements create: steward review, charity disputes and appeals (CHAR-ADR-002/006/007), independent counsel review of every eligibility rule (CHAR-ADR-010), the Nacha TPSP annual Rules Compliance Audit and Phase 2 fraud-monitoring programme, account-verification vendor minimums (two vendors behind one port per 07), a charity support desk, and media/defamation cover if anything is published.
evidence: Nacha: TPSPs must conduct an annual Rules compliance audit (Art. One 1.2.2) [ADVX-001]; Phase 2 fraud monitoring applies to each TPSP from 2026-06-19 [ADVX-002]. The lean org Model B in servicing-economics 03 has no compliance officer (only Model C, CST-R10). ADVX re-run (data/advx-sensitivity-output.csv): adding ASSUMPTION ranges anchored on cost-register rows (CST-R10 0.5-1 FTE, CST-R13 0.25-1 FTE, CST-C06 $450/h x 40-130 h, audit $8-30k, vendor minimums $0-60k, rider $0-15k) gives $176k / $316k / $509k a year (low/base/high) instead of $75k. With 20's 5-year amortisation of establishment, base per-grant cost at 70k grants becomes about $5.42 (20 says $1.98); at 700k grants $0.54 (20 says $0.20).
recommended_revision: Add a 'registry and payments-compliance operating' line (stewardship FTE, counsel, Nacha audit, vendor minimums, charity support, insurance rider) as parameters; restate per-grant Track A cost at entry scale (1-3 sponsors, 70k-210k grants); state which items are already in the servicing-economics org budget so nothing is double counted.

challenge: International grants are absent from the economics. Entry-segment single-issue and faith sponsors may need them.
evidence: 02 records RCF's 2023 policy: direct foreign grants need a $50,000 minimum and cost about $4,000 each; CNV-GRT-008 defers intermediaries and equivalency. 20 has no international line or explicit exclusion.
recommended_revision: State international as excluded from Release-1 economics, and price equivalency determination/ED or intermediary routing (CAF America-type) as pass-through when CNV-GRT-008 activates; add a demand check for target sponsors' foreign-grant share from Schedule F.

challenge: The INCLUDE_IN_FEE classification uses sponsor contribution before organisation fixed cost and build amortisation. For the first one to three sponsors, which must carry those costs, the conclusion does not survive a 10-15 bps market.
evidence: ADVX re-run (data/advx-sensitivity-output.csv, company_first_sponsor rows): for a 10k-account sponsor (base balance $206k), net of $1.66M org fixed (servicing-economics 03 base) and $1.0M a year build amortisation, payback on onboarding plus CAC is 6.8 months at 20 bps base cost and 'never' at 15, 12.5 and 10 bps. In the high cost case it is 'never' even at 20 bps. For a 1k sponsor it is 'never' at every fee. 20 discloses that contribution is before org fixed cost (section 1), but its summary and the section 4 rule read as company economics.
recommended_revision: Label INCLUDE_IN_FEE as a marginal-sponsor rule valid only once fixed costs are covered (about $1.1-1.5B operating, $1.8-2.3B fully loaded AUA per servicing-economics 10). Add a first-sponsor (design-partner) view in which onboarding is charged up front or partly funded by the sponsor.

challenge: The economics do not conform to ratified CNV-ECO-003 and CNV-ECO-005. The base case uses AI-native activity minutes (the lever case), not the no-lever C0 case. It reports no P10-P90 range. It has no pre-delegation phase (no deterministic approval, three-person release, manual NAV checks) and no stress scenarios (15% contribution decline, loss of largest sponsor, 20% renewal price pressure, December surge). It does not apply the 25% revenue-concentration cap.
evidence: CNV-ECO-003 (c5_adversarial_business.json): 'use the no-lever Unbound case (C0) as base until levers are measured', 'headline Monte Carlo P50 with the P10-P90 range', viability only if contribution margin is positive 'at P90 cost and adverse licence scale'. CNV-ECO-005 requires pre-delegation economics and the listed stresses. grep of 20 finds no C0, Monte Carlo, P90, pre-delegation or concentration treatment. Parameters ach_labour_minutes 0.1 and check_labour_minutes 1.2 come from activity-minutes-typical.csv (AI-native).
recommended_revision: Flag as a conflict with ratified clauses. Re-base on C0 activity minutes and show AI-native as a lever. Add a Monte Carlo or at least P10/P90 runs, a parameterised pre-delegation phase, and the CNV-ECO-005 stresses. Report payback at P90 cost.

challenge: Is 20 bps plausible against observed prices? It is plausible only for outsourced staffed administration at about $250-400k average balances. Many entry-segment sponsors self-staff and buy software, and for them the observed comparator is about 0.5-9 bps or $34-611 per account.
evidence: price-observations.csv: Ren staffed administration 18.4-18.8 bps at MS GIFT (re-verified: FY2024 990 RenPSG 'ADMIN & LEGAL' $14,930,249; 21,800 DAFs; $9.11B EOY [ADVX-009]), 13.3-14.1 bps at Stifel, 15.2 at CAF America/GS, 7.8 at Servant, 38-40 at USCGT/RCF. Ren software lines: 4.67 bps / $81 per account at NCF (285 employees), 5.0 / $34 at Thrivent, 3.0-9.3 elsewhere. ADVX re-run: a 10k sponsor at a $81 per-account price pays back in 20.6 months (base) and never (high cost); at $60, 57 months; at $250, 3.3 months base and 37 months high.
recommended_revision: Split the price test by buyer type: (a) outsourced administration (13-19 bps observed at large bank-channel sponsors; 20 bps is parity to slightly above); (b) self-staffed sponsors buying software (3-9 bps or about $34-326 per account). Model (b) explicitly. Adopt servicing-economics' per-account-plus-low-bps tariff as the base pricing form.

challenge: Who pays is not modelled. At the comparable sponsors, the servicer's fee is carved out of a donor-paid administrative fee schedule. Unbound's fee therefore competes with the sponsor's retained margin and with the donor's fee, not with an independent budget line.
evidence: RCF pays Ren 'based on 98% of the value of administrative fee revenue earned by the Foundation from individual fund holder accounts' ($19,225,546 in 2024) [ADVX-008]. MS GIFT's donor schedule (27/20/15/13/11/9 bps, PRC-O-004, internal; ADVX could not extract the PDF text) funds the TPA, and Ren's realised take is 18.5 bps. At MS GIFT, 20 bps would be a price increase over Ren. CNV-ECO-004: the advisor-distributed segment 'SHALL be offered on sponsor admin fees only'.
recommended_revision: Add a payer dimension: sponsor-retained margin = donor fee schedule minus servicer fee. Test Unbound's price against the incumbent servicer's realised take (for example 18.5 bps), not against list donor fees, and show the sponsor's net change.

challenge: Does the onboarding-in-fee conclusion survive a 10-15 bps market or a per-account price? It survives only as a marginal-sponsor result at 10k+ accounts in the base cost case.
evidence: ADVX re-run (fee rows): 10k sponsor, base cost: 4.3 / 3.2 / 2.6 months at 10 / 12.5 / 15 bps (INCLUDE). High cost: 106 months at 10 bps (UNECONOMIC), 33 months at 12.5 (SEPARATE), 19.5 at 15 (INCLUDE). 1k sponsor: 37 months at 10 bps (SEPARATE), 25.9 at 12.5 (SEPARATE), 19.9 at 15 (INCLUDE); high cost 'never' at every fee up to 15 bps. Per-account price: see ADVX-05.
recommended_revision: State that the conclusion holds at 10k+ accounts only under base cost assumptions. Under high cost or self-staffed software pricing, charge onboarding separately, in line with the existing gate rule.

challenge: Registry establishment competes with the core servicing build for scarce engineering. 2,600 hours (base; up to 7,600) is about 1.4 FTE-years, against a lean organisation with about 2 engineers.
evidence: 20 R2: 2,600 h base, 1,140-7,600 range. servicing-economics 03 scenario S2 has 2 engineering FTE; Unbound's own build estimate is $5M ($3-15M). UNB-CHAR-DEC-001 makes a first-party registry mandatory, so the question is scope and sequence, not whether to build. 05 specifies 3-10 state registries, deep entity resolution and six shared stores, with no release staging tied to the entry sponsor's actual recipients.
recommended_revision: Stage the registry. R1 needs federal sources (BMF, Pub 78, auto-revocation, OFAC) plus resolution of the first sponsor's actual recipient set, including the non-BMF tail. Defer state connectors beyond the first sponsor's states, generic group-subordinate resolution and open-data preparation. Tie each stage to recipients actually paid.

challenge: Would open-data distribution distract Unbound or erode incumbent advantage?
evidence: 05 already concludes that publishing 'removes almost nothing from incumbents' and defers an open dataset to post-R1, after CHAR-ADR-008 and counsel. ADVX agrees. Ren's directory claim (1.8M+) is the size of the BMF [ADVX-004]. The incumbents' scarce assets are enrolled destinations and payment volume (1.7M grants a year claimed [ADVX-004]), which open data does not touch. Residual: correction-handling and support cost if published is not costed.
recommended_revision: No change to the recommendation. If open data is reconsidered, cost corrections, support and media liability first, and require a specific acquisition benefit, for example charity claim conversion.

challenge: The package assumes that the charity network and onboarding friction are the binding competitive barriers. The evidence points more to distribution and incentive alignment: who owns the advisor and client channel, who earns the investment fee, and the incumbent's sponsor entity.
evidence: MS GIFT's FY2024 990 shows Morgan Stanley paid $4,237,948 as 'INVESTMENT ADVISOR' alongside RenPSG's $14,930,249 [ADVX-009]. Bundled affiliate lines in price-observations.csv: Thrivent affiliate 92.95 bps, T. Rowe 22.97 bps, FMR 23.72 bps. TIFIN's ADV lists 0-100 bps subadvisory fees paid to DAF advisers (repo daf-economics-and-distribution). Ren distributes through RCF white-label programmes (LPL/Commonwealth, Edward Jones, Ameriprise, Northwestern Mutual; repo ren-distribution-network, queue-vendor-channel-moves). Ren says switching providers is 'Not difficult at all' [ADVX-003]. iPhi attrition 2023-2026: 1 of 26 faith/national sponsors left; CF exits went to Foundant/akoyaGO, which fit non-DAF fund types (queue-ren-iphi-attrition). The package has no evidence that any sponsor chose or left a vendor because of its charity network or onboarding.
recommended_revision: Add an explicit buyer-decision analysis: for each entry sub-segment, list the decision maker, their economic interest (investment fee, advisor retention, sponsor margin) and switching triggers (vendor sunset, M&A, fit). Position the charity network and onboarding as necessary conditions that remove objections, not as the moat. Design for investment and custody neutrality (advisor-managed accounts, custodian feeds, CNV-GRT-009 engaged-manager programme) as the primary selling point to advisor-distributed sponsors.

challenge: Most proposed capabilities are parity: cross-sponsor ACH enrolment reuse, verify-once vetting, grant-triggered enrolment, migration services, AI or MCP charity search.
evidence: Ren: 'Charities sign up for ACH once and are digitally enabled for every DAF program we support' [ADVX-004]. Chariot verifies once for all DAF partners and holds grants 5 days with emails (08). Chariot's deposit account is 'legally owned by your organization' and 'you cannot "bring your own" bank account' [ADVX-007]. CAF America validates once (03). Migration is sold by Ren, Give, akoyaGO and Foundant (ADVB-12). The package already concedes most of this in 03, 08 and 20.
recommended_revision: Keep a capability register that marks each item parity, catch-up or differentiator. Remaining candidate differentiators: evidence-provenance decisions, charity-controlled sponsor-scoped destination evidence with no partner-account lock-in, a published migration commitment, and symmetric exit. These are HYPOTHESES until buyers rank them.

challenge: Competitive barriers that remain after all recommendations are implemented are not listed.
evidence: Residual barriers (INFERENCE): (1) wirehouse and advisor programmes sponsored by the vendor's own charity (RCF, NPT, Charityvest) are not platform migrations (10, ADVB-04); (2) affiliated investment-fee economics (ADVX-10); (3) incumbents' payment volume, 1.7M grants a year claimed (VENDOR-CLAIM [ADVX-004]), which keeps compounding enrolment; (4) Ren RDE enrolments are not portable to non-partner rails (02), so a leaving sponsor's charities re-enrol; (5) the buyer's own switching TCO of $170k-846k base (20 R17) and project capacity; (6) no references, no SOC 1 Type II, and a vendor whose survival depends on its first sponsor, against CNV-ECO-004's 25% concentration cap; (7) contractual exit-data limits at incumbents (10).
recommended_revision: Add a residual-barrier register with an owner and mitigation per item. Examples: design-partner terms with source-code or data escrow for barrier 6, a custodian/advisor integration catalogue for barrier 2, and targeted top-recipient outreach for barriers 3 and 4.

challenge: Internal inconsistency on partner coverage. 20 assumes 50% of a migrating sponsor's recipients are already enrolled with a networked partner. 08 models 2-20% per recipient and 8-21% of grants at go-live. 20 anchors its 50% on Fidelity's 67% EFT share, which is Fidelity's own enrolment, not partner coverage.
evidence: economic-parameters.csv partner_coverage 0.3/0.5/0.7 ('ECO-005; CNV-EXP-002'); 08 section 4.1 pre-enrolment 20/8/3/2% and 4.2 table; Fidelity 67% re-verified [ADVX-006]. ADVX re-run at partner_coverage 0.08: charity enrolment at onboarding for a 10k sponsor rises from $97k to $178k; payback 1.9 to 2.1 months (classification unchanged).
recommended_revision: Set partner_coverage to the 08-consistent 0.03-0.20 (base about 0.08) and remove the Fidelity anchor. The cost effect is small, but the 'network reuse' value line should be restated.

challenge: Internal inconsistency on check share. 20 values e-payment adoption at a 10% check share. 08 says 15-37% of grants are still paper after 3 years at p = 0.10-0.25, plans on p = 0.10, and Fidelity is at 33% paper after years.
evidence: economic-parameters.csv check_share_target 0.03/0.10/0.15 (ASSUMPTION). 08 section 4.3 item 3; Fidelity 67% electronic [ADVX-006]. ADVX re-run at check_share_target 0.30: combined e-pay value for a 10k sponsor falls from $75k to $9.8k a year (-87%).
recommended_revision: Set check_share_target from 08's p = 0.10 path (about 0.30-0.37 at 36 months). Restate the e-pay value lines and the '$2.29 to $1.80 per grant' claim as conditional on a measured p (CNV-ECO-003 shadow period).

challenge: The network-value claim does not match the economic outputs. Measured per-sponsor savings are small. The largest value line (sales-cycle reduction, about $0.9M) is a HYPOTHESIS, yet the summary calls the network 'mainly a sales and switching asset'.
evidence: 20 R12 at 10k accounts: e-pay savings $41k + $34k a year (about $10k after ADVX-14), enrolment avoided $48k once, sales-cycle $912k (HYPOTHESIS). Track A opex alone is $176k-509k a year after ADVX-01. At entry scale the registry and network cost more per sponsor than they measurably save. Their justification rests on unmeasured sales value and on mandatory compliance (CNV-GRT-003, UNB-CHAR-DEC-001).
recommended_revision: Reframe: the registry is a compliance cost of doing business (mandated), not a value lever. Drop or quarantine the sales-cycle value until win/loss evidence exists. Do not market network-driven savings before measurement (CNV-ECO-003).

challenge: Track B still omits operating costs that ratified clauses create: the CNV-ECO-005 pre-delegation phase (three-person release, manual NAV checks) before steady state; the CNV-ECO-003 12-month shadow replay and 90-day time study for the first paying sponsor; and post-cutover hypercare after universal credential reset.
evidence: CNV-ECO-005 and CNV-ECO-003 statement text (c5_adversarial_business.json). 10: all six donor notices reviewed reset credentials. 20 models donor contact at 10% of accounts x 15 minutes (ASSUMPTION). ADVB-05 covered rehearsals, legal, reserve and CAC but not these.
recommended_revision: Add parameters for pre-delegation duration and uplift in release labour, a first-sponsor replay/time-study cost, and a hypercare contact rate. Apply them at least to the first sponsor.

challenge: Tested and rejected: 'the unit-cost inputs for verification and rails are misquoted' and 'the average-balance input is implausible'.
evidence: Stripe: $1.50 per instant verification, $1.50 per ownership call, micro-deposits free [ADVX-005], matching ECO-003. Ren set-up 'around $50,000' and '90-120 days' [ADVX-003], matching ONB-020. The $206k base balance for the 10k sponsor sits within segment-summary.csv and below MS GIFT's about $399k, and R8 already shows the $76k low-balance case (6.5 months).
